intro_html: A proper chile relleno means roasting and peeling each pepper, stuffing it by hand, dipping it in whipped egg batter, and frying it one at a time. That is a beautiful way to spend a Sunday and a terrible way to make fourteen servings. This takes the same parts, charred peppers, spiced meat, and an absurd amount of melted cheese, and builds them into a skillet. Each serving carries 44 grams of protein and 595 calories for about $2.31.
cost_closing_html: About $2.31 a serving, and three pounds of cheese is most of that. This is not a lean dish and it was never trying to be. It is a chile relleno, and the cheese is the point.
shop_smart: Green bell peppers cost less than any other color and this recipe uses seven of them. If poblanos are close in price that week, grab them instead for a more authentic, slightly hotter result.
Cheese is the whole budget here. Compare 8 oz bags against blocks priced per pound, because at three pounds of cheese the difference adds up fast.
Char the peppers yourself under the broiler rather than buying jarred roasted peppers. Jarred costs several times as much and tastes like vinegar.
Ground turkey in the largest pack you can freeze is the other lever. Buy on sale and split it across recipes.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Halve and seed the green bell peppers, lay them cut side down on a sheet pan, and broil 8 to 10 minutes until the skins blister and blacken in patches.
Cover the hot peppers with foil for 10 minutes to steam, then slip off the loose skins and cut them into wide strips. That char is the flavor of the whole dish.
Brown the ground turkey in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high, then add the diced onion and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper and cook one minute, then sprinkle the flour over everything and stir for two minutes.
Pour in the chicken broth and simmer 5 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the meat rather than pooling around it.
Fold in the charred pepper strips and about half the Mexican cheese blend, then spread the mixture level in the skillet.
Cover with the remaining cheese and bake at 375F for 20 minutes, then broil 2 to 3 minutes until the top browns and blisters. Rest 10 minutes before portioning.
portion_html: Set the skillet on the scale, subtract the empty pan weight, and divide by 14. Cut wedges to that weight and lift them with the cheese layer intact. Each serving comes to 595 calories and 44 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Chile relleno flavor without the frying, about $2.31 a serving. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, for $1 a month.

head.description: Turkey chile relleno casserole skillet meal prep: charred peppers and spiced ground turkey under melted cheese. 595 calories, 44g protein, about $2.31 a serving.
head.keywords: chile relleno casserole, turkey skillet, tex mex casserole, charred pepper bake, high protein meal prep, cheesy turkey dinner
steps: Broil halved, seeded green peppers 8 to 10 minutes until blistered, steam under foil, peel, and slice into strips.
Brown the ground turkey in an oven-safe skillet, then cook the onion until soft.
Add garlic, chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper, then stir in the flour for two minutes.
Add the chicken broth and simmer 5 minutes until thickened, then fold in the pepper strips and half the cheese.
Top with the remaining cheese, bake at 375F for 20 minutes, broil 2 to 3 minutes, rest 10 minutes, and portion into 14 containers.
